stem:
Chipo Haulage is a transport business in Gweru. Its financial year ends on 30 June. At 1 July 2025 the motor vehicles account showed a cost of US\$167,000 and the provision for depreciation account US\$82,800. The vehicles then owned were:

| Vehicle | Cost US\$ | Date bought |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| A | 38,000 | 1 July 2022 |
| B | 33,000 | 1 July 2023 |
| C | 46,000 | 1 July 2021 |
| D | 50,000 | 1 July 2024 |

Vehicles are depreciated at 20% per annum on cost, with a full year's charge in the year of purchase and none in the year of sale.

During the year ended 30 June 2026:
- On 28 February 2026, vehicle A was traded in for a new vehicle E that cost US\$62,000. The dealer allowed US\$16,400 for vehicle A and Chipo paid the balance of US\$45,600 by bank transfer.
- On 30 April 2026, vehicle B was sold on credit to Mr Ndlovu for US\$17,400.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Calculate the accumulated depreciation, at the date of disposal, on:

parts.label: (i)
parts.stem: vehicle A
parts.explanation: Charged for 2022/23, 2023/24 and 2024/25: 3 × 7,600 = 22,800. None in the year of sale.
parts.workedSolution: 1. Charged for 2022/23, 2023/24 and 2024/25: 3 × 7,600 = 22,800. None in the year of sale.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.stem: vehicle B

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the profit or loss on disposal of:

parts.label: (i)
parts.stem: vehicle A (give the amount of the profit)
parts.explanation: Net book value 38,000 − 22,800 = 15,200. The allowance is the proceeds: 16,400 − 15,200 = profit of 1,200.
parts.workedSolution: 1. Net book value 38,000 − 22,800 = 15,200. The allowance is the proceeds: 16,400 − 15,200 = profit of 1,200.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.stem: vehicle B (give the amount of the loss)
parts.explanation: Net book value 33,000 − 13,200 = 19,800. Proceeds 17,400: loss of 2,400.
parts.workedSolution: 1. Net book value 33,000 − 13,200 = 19,800. Proceeds 17,400: loss of 2,400.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Prepare the disposal accounts for vehicle A and for vehicle B.

points.description: Vehicle A: debit motor vehicles 38,000
Vehicle A: credit provision 22,800 and motor vehicles (allowance) 16,400
Vehicle A: profit 1,200 transferred to the income statement, totals 39,200
Vehicle B: debit motor vehicles 33,000
Vehicle B: credit provision 13,200 and Mr Ndlovu 17,400
Vehicle B: loss 2,400 transferred to the income statement, totals 33,000

answerSpec.modelAnswer:
**Disposal of vehicle A account**

| Date | Details | US\$ | Date | Details | US\$ |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- | --- | ---: |
| 28 Feb 2026 | Motor vehicles | 38,000 | 28 Feb 2026 | Provision for depreciation | 22,800 |
| 30 Jun 2026 | Income statement (profit) | 1,200 | 28 Feb 2026 | Motor vehicles (trade-in allowance) | 16,400 |
|  |  | **39,200** |  |  | **39,200** |

**Disposal of vehicle B account**

| Date | Details | US\$ | Date | Details | US\$ |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- | --- | ---: |
| 30 Apr 2026 | Motor vehicles | 33,000 | 30 Apr 2026 | Provision for depreciation | 13,200 |
|  |  |  | 30 Apr 2026 | Mr Ndlovu | 17,400 |
|  |  |  | 30 Jun 2026 | Income statement (loss) | 2,400 |
|  |  | **33,000** |  |  | **33,000** |

parts.explanation: Each account has cost on the debit side, depreciation and proceeds on the credit side, and the result as the balancing figure.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Calculate the depreciation charge on motor vehicles for the year ended 30 June 2026.
parts.explanation: Vehicles A and B are sold, so no charge. C 9,200 + D 10,000 + E 12,400 (a full year on the new vehicle) = 31,600.
parts.workedSolution: 1. Vehicles A and B are sold, so no charge. C 9,200 + D 10,000 + E 12,400 (a full year on the new vehicle) = 31,600.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: Provision for depreciation and carrying amount

parts.label: (i)
parts.stem: Prepare the provision for depreciation: motor vehicles account for the year ended 30 June 2026.

points.description: Credit: balance b/d 82,800
Credit: income statement 31,600 (own figure)
Debit: disposals of vehicles A (22,800) and B (13,200)
Balance c/d 78,400 with totals agreeing and balance b/d on 1 July 2026

answerSpec.modelAnswer:
**Provision for depreciation: motor vehicles account**

| Date | Details | US\$ | Date | Details | US\$ |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- | --- | ---: |
| 28 Feb 2026 | Disposal of vehicle A | 22,800 | 1 Jul 2025 | Balance b/d | 82,800 |
| 30 Apr 2026 | Disposal of vehicle B | 13,200 | 30 Jun 2026 | Income statement | 31,600 |
| 30 Jun 2026 | Balance c/d | 78,400 |  |  |  |
|  |  | **114,400** |  |  | **114,400** |
|  |  |  | 1 Jul 2026 | Balance b/d | 78,400 |

parts.explanation: The two vehicles sold are removed from the provision and the year's charge is added.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.stem: Calculate the net book value of motor vehicles at 30 June 2026.

parts.label: (f)
parts.stem: State where the profit on the disposal of vehicle A is shown in the income statement and what it suggests about earlier depreciation.

points.description: Added to gross profit as other income
Earlier depreciation on the vehicle was too high (carrying amount was below the allowance)

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: It is shown as other income (added to gross profit). It suggests that too much depreciation was charged in earlier years.

parts.explanation: A profit on disposal is other income and corrects over-depreciation.

explanation: This ZIMSEC Paper 2 style question combines disposal accounts for a part-exchange and a credit sale with the provision for depreciation and net book value.
hints: Remember that no depreciation is charged in the year of sale.
The part-exchange allowance is treated as the proceeds of vehicle A.
A loss on disposal is the credit balancing figure.

stem:
The trial balance of Mutare Outfitters at 30 June 2025 did not agree. The debit column totalled US\$238,460 and the credit column totalled US\$239,750. The difference was entered in a suspense account. The following errors were later found:

1. The sales account was overcast by US\$1,000.
2. A discount received of US\$380 was credited to the discount received account but no entry was made in the supplier's account.
3. Wages of US\$2,450 were posted to the wages account as US\$2,540; the bank account entry was correct.
4. Equipment bought for US\$3,600 was debited to the purchases account.
5. Commission received of US\$560 was credited to the rent received account.

The draft income statement showed gross profit of US\$91,300 and net profit of US\$38,600. The draft statement of financial position showed current assets of US\$62,400 and current liabilities of US\$34,100. Ignore depreciation.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Suspense account entry

parts.label: (i)
parts.stem: Calculate the amount entered in the suspense account.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.stem: Complete the sentence.
parts.explanation: The debit column was lower than the credit column, so the suspense account was debited.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Identify the type of each error.
parts.explanation: 1 addition error; 2 one-sided entry (only the credit was made); 3 unequal debit and credit amounts; 4 principle (capital item treated as an expense); 5 commission (wrong account of the same class).

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Prepare journal entries to correct the five errors. Narratives are required.

points.description: Dr Sales 1,000, Cr Suspense 1,000
Dr Creditors 380, Cr Suspense 380
Dr Suspense 90, Cr Wages 90
Dr Equipment 3,600, Cr Purchases 3,600
Dr Rent received 560, Cr Commission received 560
Narratives given for all five entries

answerSpec.modelAnswer:
**Journal**

| Date | Details | Debit US\$ | Credit US\$ |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | Sales | 1,000 |  |
|  | Suspense |  | 1,000 |
|  | *Sales account overcast by 1,000* |  |  |
| 2 | Creditors: supplier | 380 |  |
|  | Suspense |  | 380 |
|  | *Discount received credited but not debited to the supplier* |  |  |
| 3 | Suspense | 90 |  |
|  | Wages |  | 90 |
|  | *Wages of 2,450 posted as 2,540* |  |  |
| 4 | Equipment | 3,600 |  |
|  | Purchases |  | 3,600 |
|  | *Equipment wrongly debited to purchases* |  |  |
| 5 | Rent received | 560 |  |
|  | Commission received |  | 560 |
|  | *Commission received credited to rent received* |  |  |

parts.explanation: Errors 1 to 3 upset the trial balance and are corrected through suspense; errors 4 and 5 are not.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Prepare the suspense account.

points.description: Debit: trial balance difference 1,290 and wages 90
Credit: sales 1,000 and creditors 380
Totals agree at 1,380; the account is closed

answerSpec.modelAnswer:
**Suspense account**

| Date | Details | US\$ | Date | Details | US\$ |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- | --- | ---: |
| 31 Dec | Trial balance difference | 1,290 | 31 Dec | Sales | 1,000 |
| 31 Dec | Wages | 90 | 31 Dec | Creditors: supplier | 380 |
|  |  | **1,380** |  |  | **1,380** |

parts.explanation: The account balances after the errors are corrected.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: Corrected figures

parts.label: (i)
parts.stem: Calculate the corrected gross profit.
parts.explanation: Sales are lower by 1,000 and purchases lower by 3,600: 91,300 − 1,000 + 3,600 = 93,900.
parts.workedSolution: 1. Sales are lower by 1,000 and purchases lower by 3,600: 91,300 − 1,000 + 3,600 = 93,900.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.stem: Calculate the corrected net profit.
parts.explanation: 38,600 − 1,000 (sales) + 90 (wages) + 3,600 (equipment) = 41,290. Errors 2 and 5 do not change profit.
parts.workedSolution: 1. 38,600 − 1,000 (sales) + 90 (wages) + 3,600 (equipment) = 41,290. Errors 2 and 5 do not change profit.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.stem: Calculate the corrected working capital.
parts.explanation: Creditors fall by 380: current liabilities 33,720. Working capital = 62,400 − 33,720 = 28,680.
parts.workedSolution: 1. Creditors fall by 380: current liabilities 33,720. Working capital = 62,400 − 33,720 = 28,680.

parts.label: (f)
parts.stem: Explain why errors 4 and 5 were not revealed by the trial balance.

points.description: Error 4 was entered on the correct side of both accounts affected (debit purchases instead of debit equipment)
Error 5 involved a debit and credit of equal amounts to the wrong accounts, so the totals still agreed

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Both errors involved the right amounts on the right sides, but in the wrong accounts, so total debits still equalled total credits.

parts.explanation: Errors of principle and commission leave the totals equal.

explanation: This ZIMSEC Paper 2 style question uses a suspense account, correcting journals and the corrected profit and working capital.
hints: Credits exceed debits, so suspense is debited.
Only the errors that upset the trial balance go through suspense.
Errors 2 and 5 do not change profit.
